title: Joseph Swan showed a working lamp in 1879.
description:
Joseph Swan showed a working lamp in 1879. Wikipedia says that on 3 February 1879 he publicly demonstrated one to over seven hundred people. The lamp usually cited as Edison's first success was made on 19 October 1879.

Where Swan lectured, before showing the lamp in actual operation on 17 January 1879.

His home was the first with working bulbs. Wikipedia says Underhill, Low Fell, Gateshead was the world's first house to have working light bulbs installed.

His British patent came in November 1880. Wikipedia gives British Patent 4933 on 27 November 1880. The IET adds that Swan had not sought a patent covering his lamp in general terms.

Edison went to court in Britain. Grace's Guide says he brought an infringement case over Swan's patent and lost, and had to take Swan in as a partner in his British works.

The Edison and Swan United Electric Light Company, formed by merging the two British companies.

In Britain, the company name carried both inventors.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Swan: read, first part verbatim. Established the Newcastle Chemical Society lecture of 18 December 1878, the lamp shown in operation on 17 January 1879, the public demonstration to over seven hundred people on 3 February 1879, Underhill in Gateshead as the first house with working light bulbs, British Patent 4933 on 27 November 1880, and the 1883 merger.
- https://www.theiet.org/membership/library-archives/the-iet-archives/biographies/joseph-swan/: read (IET archives biography). Established lamps demonstrated in Newcastle in January 1879, a patent application in November 1880 for improved filaments, that Swan had not sought a patent covering his lamp in general terms, legal wrangling before the two British companies merged, and the Edison and Swan United Electric Light Company (Ediswan) formed on 26 October 1883.
- https://gracesguide.co.uk/Edison_and_Swan_United_Electric_Light_Co: read (Grace's Guide). Established that the lamp usually cited as Edison's first success was made on 19 October 1879, that Edison brought an infringement case in the British courts over Swan's patent and lost, and that Edison had to take Swan in as a partner in his British works.
